source: StreetSmart Form Review — Matt Croom's daily audit of every submitted form (full packet corpus)

latest.summary: 66 submissions reviewed for the Central calendar day of Wednesday 09/23/2026: 31 air job / OWL forms, 20 trailer inspections, 6 H2S Safety Supervision Daily Inspection forms, 3 field service, 2 H2S supervision, 2 confined space, 1 equipment rig-down, 1 training class.
latest.verdict: 4 items I would treat as real safety concerns, 4 forms where a stop-work or unsafe-conditions selection needs the technician's confirmation, and a set of documentation problems grouped below. Every item flagged was re-read directly from the source PDF.

concerns.title: Stop work authority actually exercised — Ralph Forbes, XTO Energy, Mustang West 8-27H, OWL submitted 11:58 AM (job 34932_1, 7:15 AM–12:00 PM). This is the one form today
concerns.text: : "Stop the job utilized because pipe was not secure with the tagline and moved around properly" Observation: "Set up exclusion zone to remove 4 inch pipe". Details: "Replace damaged pipe." Both "Unsafe conditions" and "Stop work authority utilized" are selected, and unlike the four below, the narrative names the condition. Worth a conversation with Ralph about what happened and whether the MT was told — approver of record is Larry Hendrix. As written it sits in a "what went well" box rather than anywhere an auditor would look.
concerns.quote: Stop the job utilized because pipe was not secure with the tagline and moved around properly

concerns.title: Benzene above zero, leaking casing valve, work performed off air — Jordan Lemmons, XTO Energy, Elkin Crawford 34CC 103H, job 6:58 AM–2:39 PM (34928_1). The Details field,
concerns.text: : "Disconnected well got some benzene of 0.65 from the flowline the casing valve was leaking and tried testing for benzene in the breathing area but the wind kept blowing it away so we were able to do the job without being under the air the whole time" The same form selects "Unsafe conditions" as its sole observation, with "Had a snake in the injection line tenhorn" and "Got the snakes moved and found out it wasn't a poison one". Two distinct conditions on one job. The decision to work without being under air the whole time is the part that needs review.

confirm.text: Four forms carry "Unsafe conditions" and/or "Stop work authority utilized" in the ten-item multi-select, over and above Ralph Forbes above. On three of the four, every free-text field reads positively and no condition, hazard or stop-work event is named anywhere on the form. Kelby confirmed on 09/23 that flagging these is correct and that it is a training issue — technicians should select stop-work authority only when it was actually used, and may be selecting "Unsafe conditions" because they regard any wellhead work as unsafe rather than because a specific condition arose. These need the tech to confirm intent.

Nathan Contreras — XTO, University 10-11C 3H (34944_1), 1:02 PM. Narrative: "We observed a disconnect Done on a wellhead" and "Crews verified safeguards and locks were in place prior to work, crews verified inspection dates on straps"

Jose Campos — XTO, Glass Ranch A 204H (34738_2), 12:59 PM. Narrative states the opposite of a hazard: "No hazardous readings off initial test, or first break, killed well without many issues, and were able to change well head"

Jacob Hernandez — XTO, Turner W41D 4H (34963_1), 10:40 AM. Narrative: "Job completed just as scope called for", "Great communication with crew and MY", "Reconnect of flow line. Atmospheric test conducted."

The fourth is different and I would not assume mis-selection. Ruben Rojo — XTO, Sale Ranch A #10 (34968_1), OWL 4:31 PM. "Unsafe conditions" selected, and the only narrative on the entire form is "Job was suspended reason not given by MT". The whole Win and Learn close-out is blank — What went well, the continuation, One thing we'll do better, leave-the-location and Location Name all empty. There is no positive narrative to offset the selection and no record of what was observed or why the job stopped. Job ran 12:28–4:32 PM, scoped "needs casing rubber rep". This one needs an actual answer from Ruben.
Nathan Contreras and Jose Campos both appeared on this same list on 09/22.

clean.text: Nothing requiring attention on submissions from: Luis Zarate (Powell 1807 air job and both trailer inspections), Justin Pack (H2S daily, Lipsey 1H — again the most completely filled daily of the day), Dawson Drake (both trailer inspections and the Massie 7-8 E 251 field service), Alexander Clubb (Mulva Yard), Alejandro Najar (Lane 11A 4), 1099 Hayden Haugh (First Tee 121H supervision), 1099 Rolando Flores (University 10-11C 3H), Jeremy Norris (Talco CTB air job and both Diamondback trailer moves), and Scott Croom (Exxon Mobil Kilgore H2S Clear, two students, ticket 101000-101001). The 5:00 AM trailer run out of the Andrews shop was clean across the board: Nathan Contreras, Jordan Lemmons, Michael Jobe, Larry Jaramillo, Ralph Forbes, Pablo Soto, Jacob Hernandez and Bryan Medlin, all eleven photos current on every one.

Trailer inspections are photo-based, as are the equipment sections of the H2S daily. A defect visible only in a photograph — a damaged hose, an expired extinguisher tag, a low gauge — would not surface in this review. As on 09/22, no form today records a fire extinguisher inspection or expiration date, a first aid kit date, or a 4-gas calibration date as text; all of it exists only inside images. Nothing here should be read as confirming those are current.
